title: Earth Watch: Climate Sentinel
tagline: Design an Earth observation satellite to monitor deforestation, wildfires, and ocean health.
briefing: Global climate monitoring programs urgently require high-resolution multispectral and atmospheric data. Your mission is to design, launch, and operate an Earth-observing satellite in Sun-Synchronous Orbit that delivers continuous environmental imagery within a strict $120M budget envelope.

title: Eye on the Universe: Exoplanet Hunter
tagline: Architect a deep space observatory to detect atmospheric chemical signatures on habitable-zone exoplanets.
briefing: NASA's Astrophysics Division has issued an Announcement of Opportunity (AO) for a space observatory positioned at Sun-Earth L2. The payload requires arcsecond pointing stability, extreme thermal isolation, and gigabit-per-day data downlink through the Deep Space Network.

title: Moon Scout: Artemis Water Ice Prospector
tagline: Map water-ice deposits inside permanently shadowed craters at the lunar south pole.
briefing: Future Artemis crewed surface bases require in-situ water resources. Build a lunar scout orbiter capable of enduring polar night passes, surviving the cislunar radiation environment, and penetrating shadowed crater floors with LIDAR and neutron spectroscopy.

title: StormWatch GEO: Hurricane Eye
tagline: Place a continuous geostationary weather sentinel 35,786 km above tropical storm basins.
briefing: Design a Geostationary weather satellite able to reach high-energy GTO/GEO orbit inside the outer Van Allen radiation belts while continuously streaming microwave storm soundings and optical cloud loops.

title: Magellan Redux: Venus Cloud-Piercer
tagline: Deploy Synthetic Aperture Radar to map volcanoes beneath Venus's opaque sulfuric clouds.
briefing: Orbiting at 0.72 AU bathes solar arrays in 191% sunlight while thick clouds block visible cameras. Pair active SAR radar with precision attitude wheels and active thermal louvers.

title: Ares Recon: Jezero Mineral Surveyor
tagline: Survey ancient Martian river deltas and dust storms at 1.52 AU where solar flux halves.
briefing: At Mars (43% Earth sunlight), small panels starve heavy optics. Combine outer-solar Mega Arrays or RTGs with hyperspectral geology sensors and high-gain Ka-band DSN links.

title: Psyche DSOC: Metal Core Rendezvous
tagline: Explore metallic protoplanet core 16 Psyche at 2.9 AU while pioneering deep-space optical lasers.
briefing: Voyage to the Main Asteroid Belt (12% solar flux) with a deployable Magnetometer Boom, Neutron Spectrometer, and Star Tracker-guided Deep Space Optical Laser Communications.

title: Jovian Clipper: Europa Ocean Scout
tagline: Endure intense Jovian radiation at 5.2 AU to sample subsurface saltwater ocean clues.
briefing: At Jupiter's icy moon Europa, sunlight drops to 3.7% and radiation belts fry unshielded electronics. Equip Clipper Mega Arrays or Pu-238 RTGs, Rad-Hard FPGA avionics, and magnetic/optical ocean-plume sensors.

title: Cassini Legacy: Titan Sea Explorer
tagline: Command a nuclear Pu-238 flagship through Saturn's hazy golden moon at 9.5 AU.
briefing: At 9.5 AU around Titan, sunlight plunges to 1.1%, rendering solar panels useless. Power a Flagship SAR Radar and Magnetometer Boom continuously with Quad-MMRTG Plutonium-238 batteries.

title: NASA Deep-Space Free Flight (∞ Budget)
tagline: Unlimited-budget sandbox to explore any planet, moon, asteroid, or flagship NASA architecture.
briefing: Design with infinite (∞) mission funding across Earth, Mars, Venus, Moon, Europa, Titan, 16 Psyche, and Sun-Earth L2. Equip exact NASA flagship hardware combinations, Pu-238 RTGs, optical lasers, and super-heavy SLS launchers.
